subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the importance of Oersted's experiment?

mark_split.label: A current produces a magnetic field

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are both STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: Oersted (1820) observed a compass needle deflect near a current-carrying wire; the deflection reverses when the current reverses. This was the first experimental link between electricity and magnetism.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
insider_note: The examiner wants the observation and its meaning: a current produces a magnetic field, and the field direction depends on the current direction.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Current produces a magnetic field
lines: Oersted found that when a current flows
through a conductor, a magnetic field is
A compass needle placed near the wire
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say what is produced (a magnetic field) and around what (the current-carrying conductor).
steps.why: The compass needle is the evidence: it deflects only when the current flows, so the current itself must be making a magnetic field around the wire.
common_mistakes: Saying the wire attracts the compass needle. The needle turns because of a magnetic field, not an electric pull.
Leaving out the word around — the field forms in circles around the conductor.

recall.must_convey: That a current flowing through a conductor produces a magnetic field around it.
accept: compass needle deflects near a current
reject: field direction depends on current direction

steps.memory_tip: One wire, one compass: switch the current on and the needle turns.

steps.label: Field direction follows the current
steps.mark_note: Direction and the link it proved
lines: The direction of the field depends on
The experiment showed for the first time

lines.text: A current produces a magnetic field

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The reversal test — reverse the current and the needle reverses — is what proves the field belongs to the current.
steps.why: Reversing the current reverses the deflection, so the field is not fixed in the wire — it is set by the current. That link opened the whole subject of electromagnetism.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the deflection and not saying what it proved — the link between electricity and magnetism.
Saying the field depends on the size of the compass. It depends on the current.

recall.must_convey: That the field direction depends on the current direction, and that this linked electricity and magnetism.
accept: direction of field depends on direction of current
reverse the current and the needle reverses

steps.memory_tip: Two halves: field around the current, and reverse the current to reverse the field.
